verificationTemplate:
JOINT VERIFICATION

We, {petitioner1_name} and {petitioner2_name}, the Petitioners above-named, do hereby jointly verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above joint petition are true and correct to the best of our knowledge, information and belief. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

We further state that this joint petition is presented voluntarily, without any force, fraud, coercion or undue influence.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Petitioner No. 1                    Petitioner No. 2

promptInstructions: Draft a joint petition for divorce by mutual consent under S.13B HMA (or S.28 SMA, as selected).
Tone must be neutral and non-accusatory. Both parties are co-petitioners. Avoid blame.
Plead valid marriage with date, place, ceremonies (Hindu rites for HMA / civil registration for SMA).
Plead that parties have been living separately for one year or more immediately preceding presentation of petition (mandatory under S.13B(1) / S.28(1)).
Plead that parties have not been able to live together and have mutually agreed marriage should be dissolved.
Set out brief, neutral reasons for separation (e.g., temperamental incompatibility, irreconcilable differences). Do NOT make allegations of cruelty or fault.
Record settlement terms clearly: permanent alimony / lump sum, custody and visitation, stridhan and jewellery, movable and immovable property, pending litigation to be withdrawn.
Expressly aver free consent — no force, fraud, coercion, undue influence.
If waiver of 6-month cooling-off is sought, plead grounds permitted in Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746 — long separation, settlement done, no possibility of reunion, parties' welfare.
Procedure note: First motion → 6 months minimum / 18 months maximum cooling off → second motion → decree.
Append Lawie disclaimer: 'Lawie is a drafting assistant. The advocate is responsible for legal accuracy and filing.'

sections.description: Joint petition by mutual consent — living separately for 1+ year, not able to live together, mutually agreed to dissolve
Second motion — between 6 and 18 months from first motion; court satisfies itself and passes decree
Mutual consent divorce under SMA — analogous to S.13B HMA

filing_checklist: Application for waiver of cooling-off period (if sought)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: petitioner1_name and petitioner2_name must not be empty
If waiver_of_cooling_period_sought is true, waiver_grounds must not be empty
governing_act must be HMA_1955 or SMA_1954
key_citations: Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746 — Supreme Court holds 6-month cooling-off under S.13B(2) is directory not mandatory; can be waived where reconciliation impossible
Sureshta Devi v. Om Prakash (1991) 2 SCC 25 — consent must subsist until second motion; either party can withdraw
Anil Kumar Jain v. Maya Jain (2009) 10 SCC 415 — limited application; reaffirmed Sureshta Devi
Smruti Pahariya v. Sanjay Pahariya (2009) 13 SCC 338 — court must be satisfied consent is free at second motion
